definitions.explanation: An island with no permanent human residents. Often evokes images of tropical adventures or survival scenarios, and is a popular topic in hypothetical questions and games.

examples.japanese: {無人島|むじんとう}に{流|なが}れ{着|つ}いた。
examples.english: I washed up on a deserted island.

examples.japanese: {無人島|むじんとう}に{一|ひと}つだけ{持|も}っていくなら{何|なに}がいい？
examples.english: If you could bring just one thing to a deserted island, what would it be?

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}には{約|やく}6,000の{無人島|むじんとう}があると{言|い}われている。
examples.english: It is said that there are about 6,000 uninhabited islands in Japan.

notes:
USAGE:
A common word in everyday Japanese, frequently appearing in hypothetical questions (「{無人島|むじんとう}に{一|ひと}つだけ{持|も}っていくなら？」), TV variety shows, and adventure stories. Japan actually has thousands of uninhabited islands.

FORMS:
{無人|むじん} (unmanned, uninhabited) + {島|とう} (island).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {無人島|むじんとう}に{漂着|ひょうちゃく}する (to drift ashore on an uninhabited island)
- {無人島|むじんとう}{生活|せいかつ} (life on a deserted island)
- {無人島|むじんとう}サバイバル (deserted island survival)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {離島|りとう}: remote island — may or may not be inhabited, emphasizes distance from the mainland
- {孤島|ことう}: isolated island — emphasizes isolation, may be inhabited
